newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Uruguay refinery back up in mid-March - ANCAP.
newsitem.headline: Uruguay refinery back up in mid-March - ANCAP.

text.p: Uruguay's 37,000 barrel per day (bpd) La Teja refinery is due back onstream in the second or third week of March after a maintenance shutdown, a refinery manager said on Friday.
The refinery is owned by ANCAP, the Uruguayan state oil company.

The 37,000 bpd crude distillation unit would be the first to return to service, followed by a 9,000 bpd cat cracker, a 7,000 bpd visbreaker, a 5,000 bpd desulphurisation unit and a 3,000 bpd reformer, he told Reuters by telephone.

He said the turnaround had lasted approximately 45 days and ANCAP had awarded a tender to buy 48,000 cubic metres (302,400 barrels) of products to cover the shortfall. The tender for 30,000 cubic metres (188,700 barrels) of gas oil, 16,000 cubic metres (100,800 barrels) of 95-octane gasoline and 2,000 cubic metres (12,600 barrels) of jet fuel was awarded to a supplier which he declined to name.
He said the refinery had enough crude oil to run for more than a month, but would then return to its regular purchases of between 600,000 and a million barrels every 20 days.
